question: why does a calibration model predict a consistently high or low focal for a particular static (sequence, camera) view, and can any deployable RGB cue recover that bias on a camera it has never seen?
evidence_language: ASSOCIATION / ATTRIBUTION / PREDICTIVE SIGNAL. No causal claim is made or implied.

primary_model.name: AnyCalib anycalib_gen + radial:2
primary_model.why: strongest single-family deployable baseline and verified bit-deterministic in CAM-EXP-004.1, so no run-to-run variation enters the primary target
primary_model.source: frozen CAM-EXP-004.1 predictions; no new inference

primary_target.f_ref: dataset-provided reference focal, GT_EFFECTIVE_FOCAL = GT_NATIVE_FX in the validated original-image pixel convention (CAM-EXP-002 focal_usage_audit.md)
primary_target.frames: the frozen 64-frame nested set per view
primary_target.status: ANALYSIS TARGET for attribution; not a deployment estimator
primary_target.secondary: abs(e_v) and the conventional relative focal error %

secondary_model.name: frozen E2 (exploratory ensemble)
secondary_model.status: secondary only; contains GeoCalib, which is not run-to-run deterministic. Its definition is NOT modified here.

statistical_units.never: frames are repeated observations; 64x175 is never treated as 11,200 independent samples

forbidden_features_in_primary_probe: ground-truth focal, distortion, principal point or extrinsics

outer_validation.A_LOSO: leave one sequence out, 5 folds - CONTENT/SEQUENCE SHIFT test, not a new-camera test
outer_validation.B_LOCO: leave one physical camera out, 40 folds - NEW CAMERA test and the PRIMARY decision criterion

probe.alpha_selection: GroupKFold by physical camera INSIDE the training fold only
probe.preprocessing: training-fold median imputation and standardisation only
probe.status: LINEAR PROBE DIAGNOSTIC - not a proposed calibration method

decision_thresholds_fixed_before_results.primary_criterion: Leave-One-Physical-Camera-Out, against the P0 mean-bias baseline

controls.CONSTANT_RIG_FOCAL_ORACLE: ignores the image entirely and outputs the training folds' median reference focal. Added because this rig's reference focal is nearly constant; a probe that does not beat it has not shown a calibration signal.

hypotheses.H1: the signed bias of one physical camera repeats across sequences
hypotheses.H2: physical camera identity describes more of the bias than sequence identity
hypotheses.H3: some deployable RGB scene-geometry feature is associated with the signed bias
hypotheses.H4: a usable cue must also improve prediction on a held-out physical camera
hypotheses.H5: improvement only under LOSO would point to same-rig / repeated-camera structure
hypotheses.H6: a strong oracle camera-property association that RGB cannot recover would mean the viewpoint information exists but is not recoverable by current deployable features
hypotheses.H7: if no deployable cue predicts new-camera bias, the case for hand cues (CAM-EXP-006) is strengthened
